opener_episode.title: Whatnot founder: This is the future of e-commerce (Ep 863)
opener_episode.why: It is the most recent outside-guest episode and its theme (selling high-value collectibles online through community and live drops) is exactly Avery's lane: he launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries and coined 'Click & Mortar' (social-first marketing plus curated physical pop-ups). Opener: 'Your conversation with Grant LaFontaine about the future of e-commerce got me thinking about the one category everyone said could never sell online: blue-chip art.'

angles.headline: Click & Mortar: selling blue-chip art online before anyone trusted it
angles.pitch: Avery launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries, scaled it into an eight-figure-a-year business, and coined the 'Click & Mortar' model of social-first marketing plus curated pop-ups that others have since copied.
angles.builds_on: Ep 863 Whatnot / future of e-commerce; MFM's recurring 'business ideas' brainstorms

angles.headline: The Alec Monopoly playbook: turning a street artist into a global brand
angles.pitch: How Avery developed Alec Monopoly from street artist into a global brand with sold-out shows from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, broken down as a repeatable business model the hosts can riff on.
angles.builds_on: Ep 868 '3 businesses about to blow up' style idea riffs; MFM's 'how did this become a money machine' founder stories

angles.headline: What the ultra-rich actually buy: inside celebrity art deals
angles.pitch: Avery advises celebrities, athletes and HNW buyers; he can walk through deals like placing a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024 and what it reveals about luxury buying psychology.
angles.builds_on: MFM's wealth-mechanics and '3 founders / juiciest number' formats (2026)

booking.route: No published guest form. Best documented routes: (1) warm intro via Hampton (Sam Parr's founder community; many guests are members); (2) short direct note to Sam or Shaan on X; (3) network inbox podcasts@hubspot.com, listed by third-party directories as the MFM contact (not published by the show as a guest route). Producer credited in feed listings: Arie Desormeaux (editor: Ezra Bakker Trupiano); no public email for either.
booking.contact: podcasts@hubspot.com (third-party directory listing; network-level); producer Arie Desormeaux (no public email)

format: HubSpot Media show. Mostly Sam & Shaan brainstorming; outside guests roughly every few episodes, plus a '3 founders/strangers' format of lesser-known operators sharing one striking revenue number. Video on YouTube (@MyFirstMillionPod). Episodes ~60-90 min. Remote recording is normal; in-person case by case. Guests must bring numbers and ideas, not just a life story.
red_flags: Recent feed is heavily host-only (865, 867, 868 have no outside guest), so guest slots are limited
No official guest pitch channel; HubSpot inbox is network-level and unverified as a guest route
Skews to tech/AI founders; art-world prestige alone will not land - needs hard numbers
notes: Episode dates for 865-867 come from search-result summaries of the MFM feed; Ep 863 and 868 dates unverified. Whatnot founder Grant LaFontaine episode dated 2026-09 in prior feeder research (tier2-feeders/mfm_bigdeal_ich.json). The MIT scientist's name was not confirmed.
